9960e29f5d.why: The dead 'No chromosome carries any of them' is replaced by 'Only the chromosomes of sex cells carry them' (the genes-only-in-reproductive-cells misconception, M1), truly wrong and made tempting by the stem's sex-cell scene. 'Nearly all of them came in matched pairs' fixes the lubber's unpaired accessory X (Grokipedia, Boveri-Sutton: 22 + 1 accessory, 11 bivalents). Key is Sutton's 1903 conclusion; T4 owns genes on chromosomes by the lead's ruling, and T3 mendels-peas keys Mendel's factors staying separate, not where they sit.

e9d2375855.why: The misattribution is fixed: Tjio 'studied human cells grown in the laboratory' (the cultures came from Rune Grubb's laboratory). Method true (colchicine, then a brief hypotonic, dilute salt (citrate) pretreatment, then a squash); 46 in 23 pairs; Painter's 48 stood about 30 years (NHGRI); 'Almost every whole cell' matches the paper's 'only single cases deviating'. The evenly spaced 44-46-48 is a weak middle-value pattern, and the reviser's reason for keeping it (92 defensible for cells stopped mid-division) holds. 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs is T4's by the lead's ruling; no T1-T3 final keys it.

5f2318eb1d.why: Both dead choices are replaced by misconceptions that keep both parents in play (the same genes shown differently; more genes from the parent she looks like), so the key no longer stands out; 'neither is a twin' is gone. Key true at grade level: each parent passes a random half (NGSS LS3.B), full siblings share about half their DNA (The Tech). This is the fact, not the meiosis mechanism, as the lead's genetics ruling assigns to T4. T3 mendels-peas keys one allele per pollen grain by chance and T3 two-ways keys that sexual offspring vary; neither asks why two siblings differ. Context says 'two copies of nearly every gene', clinical and correct.

dbdb780159.why: The two-defensible split (same against new kinds) is gone: all four choices ride one axis, how often. Key true: lethal mutations about 150 times the control rate (88 in 758 cultures against 1 in 947), with untreated controls (ASU Embryo Project). Wrong choices truly wrong; 'harm only the fly struck' is the body-cell-only misconception, wrong because the X-rays reached the germ line. Context's 'many of the visible ones the same' is the judge's hedged form. Radiation raising the mutation rate is keyed nowhere else; the T4 spectrum unit's X-ray question keys bone against flesh.

d6b5c6e4e0.why: 'Rubbed smooth' is replaced by 'Peaches, through a doubling of their chromosomes', truly wrong (peach and nectarine are one species with eight chromosome pairs, 2n = 16) and parallel to the key, so the choices form two pairs and the key no longer stands alone. Key true: a single recessive mutation in PpeMYB25 (Vendramin et al. 2014; Wikipedia, Peach); the plum cross is a documented myth. Close in kind to T3's teosinte, but that keys the farmers' choosing, not the mutation as the source of a new variety.
